item.title: Predictive Processing Network Symposium, Bochum, 6-8 October
item.description: We are delighted to confirm that our Predictive Processing Network Symposium will take place in Bochum from the 6th to the 8th of October. This event is funded by a DFG network grant: Research network for the Interdisciplinary Study of Predictive Processing in Memory and Perception (PPiMP) – jointly with Andrea Greve from Cambridge – We are looking forward to great talks and stimulating discussions! https://predcommlab.github.io/symposium-2026/

item.title: Fabian's paper published in PLOS Biology
item.description: How do priors influence speech processing? Do they enhance expected signals or highlight the unexpected (prediction errors)? Fabian’s computational EEG study shows: It depends…! Many congratulations to Fabian on his new paper Sensory sharpening and semantic prediction errors unify competing models of predictive processing in human speech comprehension in PLOS Biology!

item.title: Welcome Dr. Hanna Ringer and Henrik Eichhorn
item.description: A very warm welcome to Dr. Hanna Ringer and Henrik Eichhorn to join the team at the RUB!

item.title: New lab at the RUB in Bochum
item.description: We started our new lab at the RUB in Bochum. Would you be interested in working here? The core infrastructure of THINK (for human research) consists of a 3T human MRI, a High-Performance Computing Cluster, multiple laboratories, amongst others for electrophysiological and behavioral studies, EEG, and virtual reality. All current positions are filled, but if you’re interested in a Postdoc or PhD on how expectations and context shape perception, and are considering applying for your own funding, I’d be very happy to hear from you!

item.title: Annika's eye tracking paper accepted in iScience
item.description: Congratulations to Annika on the acceptance of her exciting eye tracking paper: Expectations Guide Predictive Eye Movements and Information Sampling During Face Recognition in iScience. Both predictive and active sampling were influenced by priors! Plus, we found a link between eye movements and perceptual choices!

item.description: I am now a Professor of Predictive Cognition at Ruhr University Bochum. My deepest gratitude goes to my team, colleagues, friends, and family for their support along this journey.

item.title: TRR 289 Treatment Expectation extended
item.description: We are excited to be part of the newly extended TRR 289 Treatment Expectation in a joint project with Katja Wiech! Welcome to Philipp Schumann and Mai-Carmen Requena-Komuro to join us on this exciting project! We will investigate how communication priors shape speech and pain perception in a clinical context.
